title: 1999 AHSME Problem 11
statement: The student lockers at Olympic High are numbered consecutively beginning with locker number \(1.\) The plastic digits used to number the lockers cost \(2\) cents apiece. Thus, it costs \(2\) cents to label locker number \(9\) and \(4\) cents to label locker number \(10.\) If it costs \(\$137.94\) to label all the lockers, how many lockers are there at the school?

solutions.text:
Labeling costs \(\frac{\$137.94}{\$0.02} = 6897\) digits. Lockers \(1\)-\(9\) use \(9\) digits, lockers \(10\)-\(99\) use \(2 \cdot 90 = 180\) digits, and lockers \(100\)-\(999\) use \(3 \cdot 900 = 2700\) digits.

The remaining digits number \(6897 - 2700 - 180 - 9 = 4008,\) which label \(\frac{4008}{4} = 1002\) four-digit lockers. In all there are \(999 + 1002 = 2001\) lockers.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Divide the total cost by the cost per digit to get the number of digits
Subtract the digits used by lockers \(1\)-\(9,\) \(10\)-\(99,\) and \(100\)-\(999\)
